A runs over 4n(1−)k · (n + k) samples and stores the first 2(n + k) samples (a, b) ∈ [n] × {0, 1} such that ai ≤ n + k, ∀i ∈ [k], that is, the bit b depends only on the first (k) n + k bits of x under the distribution Dplanted (x). If A encounters less than 2(n + k) samples of the above mentioned form, A outputs 1 (“planted”). Otherwise, A goes over all  the possibilities of the first n + k bits of x (2n +k possibilities in total) and checks if it could  have generated the stored samples. If there exists a y ∈ {0, 1}n +k that generated the stored samples, A outputs 1 (“planted”), otherwise A outputs 0.
